title: Unmodeled states and uncertain action outcomes in agentic scanning tunneling microscopy
authors: Siyu Cheng, Muxian Xu, Christopher Candelora, Ilija Zeljkovic
abstract: In physical experiments, interventions can alter hidden experimental states in ways that cannot be predicted in advance. Autonomous scientific agents must therefore interpret the consequences of their interventions while operating with incomplete knowledge of the experimental state. Here we investigate this problem using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) tip conditioning, traditionally a human-expert-intensive task governed by inaccessible tip apex conditions and uncertain action outcomes. We introduce quailbot, an agent harness that places the LLM inside the instrument feedback loop by linking physical interventions with experimental readbacks. After a brief apprenticeship with a human expert, frontier LLM agents autonomously completed end-to-end tip conditioning on an STM and passed an independent verification. The contingencies that arose during the experiments further exposed the limits of LLM agentic autonomy when relevant experimental states or dynamics were hidden or unmodeled. Our results show that future autonomous physical experimentation requires agents to infer hidden and unmodeled experimental states, track the outcomes of their actions, and operate within the observability and action limits of real instruments.
summary: This work demonstrates an LLM-based agent system, 'quailbot,' capable of autonomously performing complex, multi-step scientific tasks like STM tip conditioning. By integrating the LLM into the instrument's feedback loop, the agent learns to adapt to physical uncertainties and hidden experimental states. It advances the field by showing how AI can manage real-world, unpredictable physical measurements.
main_problem: Autonomous scientific agents must interpret the consequences of their interventions when operating with incomplete knowledge of the experimental state, especially when interventions alter hidden states unpredictably.
main_result: LLM agents successfully completed end-to-end STM tip conditioning after apprenticeship, demonstrating adaptation to unexpected physical conditions.
method: The authors developed 'quailbot,' an agent harness that embeds an LLM into the instrument feedback loop to link physical interventions with experimental readbacks.
model_or_system: The physical system is Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) tip conditioning on FeTe at 4 K. The agent interacts with the instrument using CLI tools to control physical parameters.
key_observables: BraggZ score, topographs, Fourier transforms, and tunneling current are used to diagnose tip quality and surface structure.
important_parameters: The experiment operates under conditions of hidden states (e.g., tip apex configuration) and unmodeled latent contingencies.
main_assumptions: The primary limitation is that the agent's autonomy is constrained by the observability and action limits of the real instrument, and it struggles when states are hidden or unmodeled.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of public vs. hidden states in tip conditioning, the architecture of the quailbot harness, and the sequence of agent actions during a successful run.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of action-outcome uncertainty in physical experiments, details the quailbot agent harness and its apprenticeship training, presents results showing autonomous completion of STM tip conditioning, and concludes by discussing the necessity of inferring hidden states.
why_interesting: While the focus is on AI control, the underlying physical measurements (STM, lattice structure, correlated materials) are highly relevant to condensed matter physics, particularly in characterizing electronic states.
